video_specification.overview:
Produce a {DURATION_SECONDS}-second {TONE} video about {TOPIC}. The final deliverable is a rendered MP4 at 1920x1080 30fps generated by Remotion, with continuous narration synthesized via ElevenLabs.
Visual style: {VISUAL_STYLE}. Every frame has continuous motion — no static frames. No on-screen text mirrors the voiceover at any point; the audience hears the words and watches the visuals, not both at once.

prerequisites.environment_setup: - ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is exported in the shell environment - ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID optionally overrides the default voice (Rachel) - Node 20+ and pnpm are available - The Remotion project is pre-scaffolded by the harness driver with package.json, tsconfig.json, src/Root.tsx (placeholder), src/anchors.ts (stub), src/shots/ (empty), public/, vitest.config.ts. Do not touch package.json dependencies.

technology_stack.audio_format: MP3 from ElevenLabs, served from public/audio.mp3
technology_stack.captions: NONE — there are no on-screen captions or subtitles

pacing_rules.rule: Every frame must have continuous motion. Static frames are forbidden.
No on-screen text mirrors the voiceover. The viewer hears the words; they should not also read them. Diagram labels and numerical callouts are fine; sentences from the narration are not.

Shots and transitions are determined by the rhythm of the spoken narration. A complete declarative statement is a shot. A connecting clause or bridging idea is a transition. A punchy single word can be its own shot. Phase A (the director) decides where the cuts land based on how the spoken line wants to breathe.

Shot complexity (`simple` vs `complex`) is derived from each shot's actual duration after TTS. Shot agents use it as a hint for visual density: longer shots get layered animations, shorter shots get single-element motion.

video_specification.narrative_arc:
{NARRATIVE_ARC_PROSE}
Three to five sentences describing what the audience learns and in what order. This is the input to Phase A which writes the continuous narration AND decides phrase boundaries (shots vs transitions). Do NOT write the literal voiceover here.
video_specification.pacing_hints:
{OPTIONAL_PACING_HINTS_FROM_BRIEF}
Examples: "punchy short phrases", "slow contemplative build", "data-heavy with frequent cuts", "single-word emphasis on the payoff". Phase A reads these as guidance, not commands.

step.title: Phase A — Director
step.tasks: - Read video_spec.xml - Write script.json with continuous narration + phrases (each marked role=shot or role=transition by char range) + optional anchors - Stop

step.title: TTS
step.tasks: - Driver synthesizes the narration via ElevenLabs and uses the per-character alignment to convert each phrase's char range into a frame range, producing timing.json with shots[]

step.title: Phase B — Shot components (parallel, max 5 concurrent)
step.tasks: - One shot agent per timing.shots[i] - Each writes src/shots/Shot{NN}.tsx + Shot{NN}.anchors.json - Continuous motion. No on-screen text mirroring the voiceover.

step.title: Phase C — Compositor
step.tasks: - Assemble src/Root.tsx with Audio + shot Sequences (no captions) - Run vitest alignment test - Run `npx remotion render` → out/video.mp4

success_criteria.functionality: - alignment.test.ts passes - out/video.mp4 exists and plays end-to-end - No on-screen text mirrors the voiceover - No static frames - Cuts land on the rhythm of the spoken narration, not on arbitrary visual boundaries
